findings.where: First screen, desktop: the handwritten red "write to me" note in the left margin, next to the hero
findings.fault: The page's one action is the lightest thing in the first screen. It is a small scribble outside the red margin line, sitting on its own below the hero lines and away from the headline, the clipped photograph and the large aqueduct drawing. When you squint, all three of those come first, and the note reads as a doodle beside the text, not as the way to reach Mark.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff who arrive wanting to contact the advisor. They read the headline and the photograph, look to the right and down at the drawing, and may never take the margin scribble for the contact route. The main nav item, 'Contact', doesn't help either: it uses a different label and goes nowhere yet (#).

findings.where: Article specimen, the closing row "Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge — Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF" (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Only the title is a link. Its only link cue is a full-width table rule that runs under the static "Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF" text as well as the title. So the line looks like a divider rather than a link underline, and it underlines plain text that does nothing. Nothing says that the bold title in particular opens the PDF.
findings.who_objects: A reader who wants Mark's lecture. They can't tell whether the row opens, and if they click the underlined date or 'PDF' text, nothing happens. Angélique will add a row like this every time she posts a PDF, so the confusion would recur all through the article pages.

findings.where: Motion sketch panel, "Replay the note" (a button), compared with the text links on the page
findings.fault: The button is drawn as an underlined text link, which is the look that means a link elsewhere on the page. So the underline means both 'go somewhere' and 'do something here'.
findings.who_objects: Anyone using the tile who expects an underlined phrase to take them somewhere. Here it replays an animation in place instead, which is a small surprise and blurs which look means which function for the layout round that builds on this tile.
